Add job details to every row: job id, file name, Document Definition and processed time. Then each job’s data can be filtered or exported on its own. This is what I’d recommend instead of a separate database per job: a database per job is hard to query, back up and manage.
Don’t let one unexpected definition block the job: let “Tables by Document Definition” skip a definition with no tables set up, and flag it on the job page instead of failing the whole stage.
Choose what happens when a file is processed again: keep the old row (today’s behaviour), or update it with the new values.

Choosing a definition: let a FlexCapture stage specify which definition(s) are allowed, send ?definition= to the bridge, and understand the two new error codes. A definition mismatch should count as “not this project”, so the all-projects search moves on.

"In jobs" count: the card says 1,001 files are in jobs, but 100 of them are in part 11, which hasn't started yet. I can make that count only files whose job has actually started.

Multi-page PDFs overwrite their own raw OCR output. I found this in my first review: the raw-output file path in workflows/ocr.go has no page number, so for a 16-page PDF only one page's raw result survives. vol4 is almost all multi-page PDFs. The extracted text in the database is fine; it's the stored raw response per page that gets lost.
Remove or repair cmd/worker. Earlier today it silently failed every job. At minimum, add a test that it registers the same steps as the all-in-one server.
Automatic retry after an outage. Pages that failed with "unavailable" (49 in today's run) should be retried once the OCR service is back, without anyone pressing Retry.

7. Throughput and failure dashboard: pages per minute, queue depth, OCR response times, failures by type, and an estimated finish time per import. Everything I measured with scripts today should be on a page.
